title: Targeted Capture Method Using BAC Libraries for Sequencing Large Genes
author: Kae Koganebuchi
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qpndvme
materials: The concentration was measured using a NanoPhotometer (Implen).
The sheared BACs were purified using a MinElute PCR Purification Kit (Qiagen).
1.5-μg sheared BACs per capture reaction were prepared.
Blocking oligonucleotide solutions (Maricic et al., 2010) and human Cot-1 DNA were added to the library solution.
Following incubation, Dynabeads M-270 Streptavidin (Invitrogen; CA, USA) was added to the hybridization mixture.
The PCR amplicon was purified using a MinElute PCR Purification Kit (Qiagen).

steps.title: Purify BAC DNA
steps.instruction: Purify the BAC using the NucleoBond BAC 100 kit (Macherey‑Nagel, Düren, Germany) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Shear BAC to target size
steps.instruction: Shear 5 µg of purified BAC on a Covaris S2 sonicator (Covaris) using default settings to obtain fragments ranging from 350 to 750 bp.

steps.title: Biotinylate sheared DNA
steps.instruction: Biotinylate the sheared DNA following the protocol described in Maricic et al. (2010).

steps.title: Dry biotinylated DNA
steps.instruction: Dry the biotinylated DNA solution in a heat block set to 95 °C until all liquid is evaporated.

steps.title: Add hybridization reagents
steps.instruction: Add hybridization buffer and formamide to the dried DNA and suspend the mixture by vortexing.

steps.title: Denature DNA
steps.instruction: Denature the suspension by heating at 95 °C for 10 min in a heat block to generate single‑stranded DNA.

steps.title: Add biotinylated BAC baits
steps.instruction: Add 500 ng of biotinylated BAC baits (eluted in 4.5 µL PCR‑grade water) to the single‑stranded DNA mixture and mix by pipetting.

steps.title: Hybridization incubation
steps.instruction: Place the mixture in a thermal cycler, heat to 95 °C for 10 min, then incubate at 65 °C overnight (12–16 h).

steps.title: Wash and elute captured DNA
steps.instruction: Capture the biotin‑bound DNA fragments with NGS MagnaStand (Nippon Genetics, Tokyo, Japan), then wash and elute according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: First post‑capture PCR
steps.instruction: Perform PCR on the enriched library: (a) run a preliminary PCR on 26 µL of the enriched library before magnetic‑bead removal; (b) use 5 µL of the eluted library as template in a 50 µL reaction containing 0.3 mM dNTPs, 0.5 µM each Sol_bridge_P5 and Sol_bridge_P7 primer (per Maricic et al.), and 1.0 U KAPA HiFi DNA Polymerase. Cycle: 98 °C 2 min initial denaturation, then 8 cycles of 98 °C 10 s, 60 °C 15 s, 68 °C 50 s.

substeps.instruction: Run a preliminary PCR on 26 µL enriched library before bead removal
Set up 50 µL PCR with 5 µL eluted library as template, 0.3 mM dNTPs, 0.5 µM each primer, 1.0 U KAPA HiFi polymerase
Thermal cycling: 98 °C 2 min; 8 × (98 °C 10 s, 60 °C 15 s, 68 °C 50 s)

steps.title: Second capture
steps.instruction: Repeat the capture procedure (steps 5–9) using the purified first‑post‑capture library as input.

steps.title: Second post‑capture PCR
steps.instruction: Perform a second post‑capture PCR on the second‑capture library using the same reaction mix as in step 10, but with 13 amplification cycles under the same thermal profile.

substeps.instruction: Set up 50 µL PCR with the same components as step 10
Thermal cycling: 98 °C 2 min; 13 × (98 °C 10 s, 60 °C 15 s, 68 °C 50 s)

steps.title: Quantify final library
steps.instruction: Quantify the amplified capture library with a KAPA Library Quantification Kit for Illumina NGS platforms and assess fragment size distribution on an Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer.
